brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: 3x full bases in L-cluster (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full) with top covers, ~310x310mm deck (f13) – capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied.
notch:0#-1,1#notch0 hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf installed between two cells, providing pull-out drawer compartments.

requirements.requirement: Spike at corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 mount spike at junction of the three bases (0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0) – the only triple junction offered.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on mount spike – small flat working surface for light items.

finish.summary: Built compact L-shaped 3-cell desk unit with top covers, a notch drawer (mf) and a mount spike at the triple junction (0,0/0,1/1,0) carrying a small platform. House rules run (capOpenFaces, lockJoints); meshClash clear. Dressed with pencil cup on deck and pen in drawer to show desk use.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
